diagnosis: The model repeatedly suffers high loss because it assumes linear narrative continuation (e.g., escalating disputes, detailed supply-chain impacts) when the true next article is often off-topic—a local crime story, a commemorative piece, a policy bill, or a different company's announcement. It also over-specifies events (e.g., WTO complaints, specific talks) even when historical news is ambiguous or already shows de-escalation attempts. The guidance already mentions off-topic possibilities, but the examples show the model still fails to assign sufficient probability to topic shifts.
suggestions: When historical news compresses many entries on a single narrow event (e.g., Nexperia standoff, automaker chip crisis), explicitly assign high probability to the next article being completely off-topic—an unrelated local news story, a different industry announcement, or a human-interest piece—rather than continuing the same narrative.

If the historical news contains any off-topic articles interspersed (e.g., school hiring, soldier mourning, lodge legacy), treat those as strong signals that the sequence is not purely thematic; predict tone-neutral or constructive descriptions for the next article if it returns to the main topic, but default to expecting a different subject entirely.
